newsitem.title: USA: Centennial, once a star, seen sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Centennial, once a star, seen sharply lower.

text.p: Shares of Centennial Technologies Inc, which rose a phenomenal 451 percent in 1996, were expected to open sharply lower after the company fired its chairman and questioned the accuracy of past financial statements.
Shares of the maker of cards for computers and contract manufacturing services closed at 16-3/8 on Monday, but have not yet opened on the New York Stock Exchange.
Market analysts expect it to open sharply lower, with one trader speculating it could open near $5 a share.
It is a stunning turnaround at a company that rose 451.0 percent in 1996, based on its closing price of $9.44 at year-end 1995 and $52 at year-end 1996.
The former market darling said it is checking the accuracy of earnings for the quarter ended December 31 and prior statements that could contain material misstatements.

It fired its chairman, chief executive and secretary Emanual Pinez and said chief financial officer James Murphy is being relieved of his duties until further notice. Murphy is assisting the company in its inquiry, Centennial said.
An article late last month that appeared in FinancialWorld questioned the company's accounting practices.
